messages.text:
"Create a basic 2D top-down survival and exploration game set in \"La Franja Roja\", a post-apocalyptic version of Chile after a nuclear war between the United States, the Soviet Union and their allies.

WORLD:
The game takes place in central Chile, in a devastated landscape of abandoned towns, ruined roads, forests, rural settlements and contaminated areas. The north is heavily irradiated, the center is a dangerous wasteland, and the south remains relatively habitable.

ART STYLE:
Pixel art, dark and atmospheric visuals. Use recognizable Chilean and Latin American architecture, abandoned houses, rural roads, improvised shelters and damaged infrastructure. Avoid futuristic or American post-apocalyptic aesthetics.

GAMEPLAY:

- Top-down player movement.
- Explore a small open map.
- Collect food, water, scrap and useful equipment.
- Manage health, hunger and thirst.
- Interact with NPCs through dialogue.
- Trade resources with survivors.
- Find abandoned buildings and loot containers.
- Avoid contaminated areas and environmental hazards.
- Include a simple day and night cycle.

PLAYER:
The player starts with basic supplies in an abandoned rural settlement. They must explore, gather resources and survive.

ENVIRONMENT:
Include abandoned vehicles, ruined buildings, improvised survivor camps, forests, contaminated zones and scattered environmental storytelling.

GAME SYSTEMS:
Create a functional inventory, health system, resource collection, basic trading and simple NPC interactions. Display player statistics on the interface.

DESIGN:
Keep the game small, playable and technically simple. Prioritize functional mechanics over complex graphics. Create a complete playable prototype with a clear beginning and no mandatory main quest.

ATMOSPHERE:
Focus on isolation, uncertainty, scarcity and everyday survival. The world should feel abandoned but not completely lifeless. Avoid excessive combat, zombies, futuristic weapons and generic apocalypse clichés.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
